content:
Webb County is keeping its hospital fee at 6%, a rate that brings in nearly $40 million a year for low-income health care, according to KGNS.

The money flows through the Local Provider Participation Fund, which began in 2013. Under the fund, private hospitals pay in, and the money pays for medical care for eligible low-income residents, KGNS reported.

Both Laredo Medical Center and Doctors Hospital told commissioners they support the fee during a Commissioners Court meeting on Monday, October 26, according to KGNS. Laredo Medical Center CEO Jorge Leal told the court the program is a major part of the hospital's work and thanked the county health services team, KGNS reported.

Webb County Public Health Services Executive Director Nancy Cadena also told commissioners about a change in state rules, according to KGNS. Under the change, payments for inpatient and outpatient care are split, and the county will open a new bank account to keep those payments separate going forward.

Sources:

  • KGNS, “Webb County renews provider fund supporting low-income patients,” October 28, 2026
